description: We're Team Interstellar from IST Islamabad and building a public web tool that lets anyone flip between SPHEREx sky images over time, spot moving objects like asteroids and comets, and instantly check whether they're already known. Think of the blink comparator that found Pluto, rebuilt for the infrared sky.
summary: MIDAAR is an explorable universe with NASA’s SPHEREx telescope data built in. Fly from the real Earth to any of 59,000 real stars, press one button, and see real SPHEREx infrared pictures of that star placed in the sky. Only same-colour pictures are compared, so what changes is a real change, and candidate movers are circled as leads, never discoveries.
details:
SPHEREx maps the whole sky in 102 infrared colours, and a patch of sky lands on a different colour at every visit. A plain flip-book of its pictures therefore confuses motion, brightness change and colour change. MIDAAR reads the exact colour of each picture at your target and compares only pictures of the same colour. It refuses any other comparison and says why.

You start in space on the real Earth, with SPHEREx at true size in its orbit, and fly to any of 59,119 real Gaia stars. At Barnard’s Star, one button places the real SPHEREx pictures in the sky at the star’s true direction and distance. You can scrub through time, see the difference between dates, and orbit around the pictures in 3D. In the Movie view, candidates are circled, checked against known asteroids, and guarded against glare near saturated stars.

Eleven cards add flags read by name, a quick-look 102-colour spectrum, six detector-array co-adds, Gaia and WISE overlays, brightness over time, a significance check, and a sourced comparison with other observatories. All five challenge places (Barnard’s Star, Epsilon Indi, WISE 0855, RW Aurigae, R Draconis) work completely offline. Every view is a link, it can be embedded, and it runs on a phone.

What we tested: 117 backend tests and 42 browser tests pass, and all five places pass with the internet blocked.

What did not work, reported honestly: Barnard’s Star saturates SPHEREx, so no proper motion could be fitted. WISE 0855 was not detected in two frames. A colour-model differencing idea failed validation and is not offered. Films for other stars need the live archive.

How NASA data is used

  • NASA SPHEREx images, DR1 and QR3, and the all-sky cube (IRSA): the core. Every film, difference, flag, spectrum and detector view is built from them.
  • AllWISE and 2MASS (IRSA): infrared brightness for 53,404 stars and the overlay.
  • ESA Gaia DR3: positions, motions and distances for 59,119 stars.
  • JPL orbital elements and IAU values: the planets in the 3D view.
  • Also used: SIMBAD, SkyBoT and Celestrak. Astropy and Aladin Lite are used as the brief suggests.
